sessions.title: Upper 1
warmup: 5 minutes of easy walking, cycling or rowing, just enough to feel warm
Arm circles and shoulder rolls, 10 each way
10 band pull-aparts or wall slides, and 10 slow push-ups on a wall or bench
Before your first lift: one light set of 10, then one of 5 at about 70 percent of your working weight

exercises.name: Chest press machine
exercises.cue: Seat height so the handles are at mid-chest. Press forward without locking out, return slowly.

form.setup: Shoulder blades pulled back and down, feet planted, hands just wider than your shoulders.
form.move: Lower to mid-chest under control, then press up and slightly back toward your face.
form.breathe: In as you lower, out as you press.
form.avoid: Flaring elbows straight out, bouncing off your chest, or lifting your hips.

exercises.progress: When every set reaches 12 reps with 3 left, add the smallest weight step and start again at 8.
exercises.weightHint: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 3 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

busy.name: Dumbbell bench press
busy.cue: Shoulder blades pinched back and down, feet planted. Lower to the line of your chest, then press up and slightly in.
busy.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
busy.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

busy.name: Smith machine bench press
busy.cue: Bench placed so the bar lowers to mid-chest. Press up in a straight line.
busy.why: Machine: guided and easy to set up
busy.hint: Start about 20 percent lighter and find your weight in two warm-up sets.

busy.name: Incline push-up (hands on a bench or counter)
busy.cue: The higher your hands, the easier it is. Lower the height over the weeks until you can do floor push-ups.
busy.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
busy.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

dumbbellOnly.name: Dumbbell bench press
dumbbellOnly.cue: Shoulder blades pinched back and down, feet planted. Lower to the line of your chest, then press up and slightly in.
dumbbellOnly.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
dumbbellOnly.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

home.name: Incline push-up (hands on a bench or counter)
home.cue: The higher your hands, the easier it is. Lower the height over the weeks until you can do floor push-ups.
home.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
home.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

next.note: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 3 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

exercises.name: Seated cable row
exercises.cue: Chest tall. Pull the handle to your belly button, squeeze your shoulder blades, return with control and do not rock.

form.setup: Chest tall, shoulders down, a flat back, arms reaching forward.
form.move: Pull your elbows back past your ribs, squeeze your shoulder blades, then return with control.
form.avoid: Rounding your back or shrugging toward your ears.

exercises.progress: When every set reaches 12 reps with 3 left, add the smallest weight step and start again at 8.
exercises.weightHint: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 3 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

busy.name: Chest-supported row machine
busy.cue: Chest on the pad. Pull your elbows back past your body and squeeze, return slowly.
busy.why: Machine: guided and easy to set up
busy.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

busy.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row (incline bench)
busy.cue: Chest on a bench set at an incline. Row both dumbbells toward your hips and squeeze.
busy.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
busy.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

busy.name: Inverted row (sturdy table or low bar)
busy.cue: Lie under a very sturdy table or low bar and pull your chest up with a straight body. Only use a table that cannot tip or slide.
busy.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
busy.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

dumbbellOnly.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row (incline bench)
dumbbellOnly.cue: Chest on a bench set at an incline. Row both dumbbells toward your hips and squeeze.
dumbbellOnly.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
dumbbellOnly.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

home.name: One-arm row with a bag or water can (hand on a chair)
home.cue: One hand and one knee on a chair or bed. Row a loaded bag or water can to your hip.
home.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
home.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

harder.name: One-arm dumbbell row (hand on a bench)

next.note: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 3 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

exercises.name: Shoulder press machine
exercises.cue: Seat so the handles start at shoulder height. Press up without locking out, lower slowly.

form.setup: Ribs down, glutes tight, hands just outside your shoulders, forearms vertical.
form.move: Press straight up until your arms are almost straight, then lower to shoulder height.
form.avoid: Leaning back or shrugging at the top.

exercises.progress: When every set reaches 12 reps with 3 left, add the smallest weight step and start again at 8.
exercises.weightHint: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 3 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

busy.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
busy.cue: Sit with back support if you can. Press until your arms are nearly straight. Keep your ribs down and do not arch your lower back.
busy.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
busy.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

busy.name: Pike push-up
busy.cue: Hips high, hands on the floor. Lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands, then push back.
busy.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
busy.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

busy.name: Landmine press
busy.cue: One end of the bar in a corner or landmine base. Press up and forward in a natural arc. Kind to most shoulders.
busy.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
busy.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

dumbbellOnly.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
dumbbellOnly.cue: Sit with back support if you can. Press until your arms are nearly straight. Keep your ribs down and do not arch your lower back.
dumbbellOnly.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
dumbbellOnly.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

home.name: Backpack overhead press
home.cue: Hold a loaded backpack by the handle or at your shoulders with both hands and press it overhead.
home.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
home.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

next.note: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 3 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.cue: Grip a little wider than your shoulders and lean back slightly. Pull the bar to your upper chest with your elbows going down and back.

form.setup: Chest tall, a small lean back, grip a little wider than your shoulders.
form.move: Pull your elbows down toward your ribs until the bar reaches your upper chest. Let your arms rise back up slowly.
form.avoid: Pulling behind your neck or swinging your whole body.

exercises.progress: When every set reaches 12 reps with 3 left, add the smallest weight step and start again at 8.
exercises.weightHint: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 3 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

busy.name: Close-grip (V-handle) pulldown
busy.cue: Chest tall, pull the handle to your upper chest and squeeze your lats.
busy.why: Cable: smooth, constant tension
busy.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

busy.name: Assisted pull-up machine
busy.cue: Choose enough assistance for 8 clean reps. Start from straight arms, pull your chest to the bar.
busy.why: Machine: guided and easy to set up
busy.hint: Start about 20 percent lighter and find your weight in two warm-up sets.

busy.name: Slow-lowering pull-up
busy.cue: Step or jump to the top position and lower yourself for four to five seconds. Builds the strength for a full pull-up.
busy.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
busy.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

home.name: Superman pulldown (lying on the floor)
home.cue: Lie face down with arms overhead. Lift your chest slightly and sweep your elbows down to your ribs, squeezing your back.
home.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
home.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

next.note: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 3 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

exercises.name: Reverse pec deck (rear shoulder fly)
exercises.cue: Chest on the pad, arms level with your shoulders. Open your arms wide by squeezing your shoulder blades together.

form.setup: Hinge forward with a flat back, arms hanging, neck long.
form.move: Pull your elbows out and back, squeezing between your shoulder blades, then lower slowly.
form.avoid: Using momentum or shrugging.

exercises.progress: When every set reaches 20 reps with 2 left, add the smallest weight step and start again at 12.
exercises.weightHint: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 2 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

busy.name: Cable face pull
busy.cue: Rope at face height. Pull toward your forehead with high elbows and rotate your hands outward at the end.
busy.why: Cable: smooth, constant tension
busy.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

busy.name: Chest-supported rear fly (incline bench)
busy.cue: Chest on a bench set at an incline. Open the dumbbells out to the side with soft elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades.
busy.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
busy.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

busy.name: Prone Y-T-W raise
busy.cue: Lie face down on the floor or a bed. Lift your arms in a Y, a T, then a W, thumbs up, squeezing your shoulder blades.
busy.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
busy.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

dumbbellOnly.name: Chest-supported rear fly (incline bench)
dumbbellOnly.cue: Chest on a bench set at an incline. Open the dumbbells out to the side with soft elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades.
dumbbellOnly.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
dumbbellOnly.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

home.name: Prone Y-T-W raise
home.cue: Lie face down on the floor or a bed. Lift your arms in a Y, a T, then a W, thumbs up, squeezing your shoulder blades.
home.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
home.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

next.note: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 2 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
exercises.cue: A slight bend in your elbows. Lift out to shoulder height only, lead with your elbows, lower slowly. Light weight, high control.

form.setup: Slight forward lean, a soft bend in the elbows, weights at your sides.
form.move: Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, lead with your elbows, lower slowly.
form.avoid: Swinging your body or lifting above shoulder height.

exercises.progress: When every set reaches 20 reps with 2 left, add the smallest weight step and start again at 12.
exercises.weightHint: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 2 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

busy.name: Cable lateral raise
busy.cue: Pulley low, work one arm at a time. Lift out to shoulder height with a soft elbow and lower slowly.
busy.why: Cable: smooth, constant tension
busy.hint: Machines feel lighter. Find your weight in two warm-up sets, then stay with the same reps.

busy.name: Lateral raise machine
busy.cue: Pads against your arms. Raise to shoulder height and lower slowly.
busy.why: Machine: guided and easy to set up
busy.hint: Machines feel lighter. Find your weight in two warm-up sets, then stay with the same reps.

home.name: Lateral raise with water bottles or bags
home.cue: Fill two bottles or hold two small bags. Same movement as a dumbbell lateral raise.
home.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
home.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

next.note: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 2 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

exercises.name: Dumbbell biceps curl
exercises.cue: Elbows by your sides. Curl up, squeeze, lower for two to three seconds. No swinging.

form.setup: Elbows pinned beside your ribs, shoulders relaxed.
form.move: Curl up, squeeze for a moment, and lower for 2 to 3 seconds.
form.avoid: Swinging your back or letting your elbows move forward.

exercises.progress: When every set reaches 15 reps with 2 left, add the smallest weight step and start again at 10.
exercises.weightHint: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 2 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

busy.name: Hammer curl
busy.cue: Palms facing each other. Curl up and lower slowly. Good for the forearm and upper arm together.
busy.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
busy.hint: Start about 20 percent lighter and find your weight in two warm-up sets.

busy.name: Cable biceps curl
busy.cue: Elbows by your sides, curl the handle up and lower slowly with constant tension.
busy.why: Cable: smooth, constant tension
busy.hint: Machines feel lighter. Find your weight in two warm-up sets, then stay with the same reps.

busy.name: Preacher curl machine
busy.cue: Upper arms flat on the pad. Curl up and lower fully under control.
busy.why: Machine: guided and easy to set up
busy.hint: Machines feel lighter. Find your weight in two warm-up sets, then stay with the same reps.

dumbbellOnly.name: Hammer curl
dumbbellOnly.cue: Palms facing each other. Curl up and lower slowly. Good for the forearm and upper arm together.
dumbbellOnly.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
dumbbellOnly.hint: Start about 20 percent lighter and find your weight in two warm-up sets.

home.name: Backpack or water-can curl
home.cue: Hold a loaded backpack by the handle or a filled can. Curl up and lower slowly.
home.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
home.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

exercises.name: Goblet squat (dumbbell)
exercises.cue: Hold one dumbbell at your chest. Sit down between your heels with your chest tall, then stand up.

form.setup: Feet about shoulder-width, toes turned out a little. Chest tall, eyes forward.
form.move: Sit down and back between your heels until your thighs are about parallel, then push the floor away.
form.breathe: In on the way down, out as you stand.
form.avoid: Knees caving in, heels lifting, or your chest dropping forward.

exercises.progress: When every set reaches 12 reps with 3 left, add the smallest weight step and start again at 8.
exercises.weightHint: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 3 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

busy.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
busy.hint: Start about 20 percent lighter and find your weight in two warm-up sets.

busy.name: Leg press
busy.cue: Feet shoulder-width on the middle of the platform. Lower until your knees are about 90 degrees with your hips on the seat. Do not lock your knees at the top.
busy.why: Machine: guided and easy to set up
busy.hint: Machines feel lighter. Find your weight in two warm-up sets, then stay with the same reps.

busy.name: Box squat (to a bench or chair)
busy.cue: Sit back to a sturdy bench or chair, touch it lightly without dropping onto it, then stand up. Hold a weight at your chest to make it harder.
busy.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
busy.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

home.name: Box squat (to a bench or chair)

home.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
home.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

exercises.name: Cable pull-through
exercises.cue: Face away from the cable with the rope between your legs. Push your hips back with a flat back, then squeeze your glutes to stand tall.

form.setup: Feet hip-width, soft knees, weight on the middle of your feet.
form.move: Push your hips back like closing a car door with them. Keep the weight close to your legs, then squeeze your glutes to stand.
form.breathe: In as you lower, out as you stand.
form.avoid: Rounding your lower back or turning it into a squat.

exercises.progress: When every set reaches 12 reps with 3 left, add the smallest weight step and start again at 8.
exercises.weightHint: Find a weight where the last rep of the last set still leaves 3 in the tank. Warm up with one lighter set first.

busy.name: 45-degree back extension (glute focus)

busy.why: Machine: guided and easy to set up
busy.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

busy.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
busy.cue: Hinge forward on one leg with the other leg reaching back, hips square. Touch a wall or chair for balance if you need to.
busy.why: Free weights: needs a little more balance and control
busy.hint: Start about 30 percent lighter. Free weights ask more of your balance.

busy.name: Glute bridge
busy.cue: Lie on your back, feet flat. Push your hips up until your body is in a line, squeeze, lower slowly. Rest a dumbbell or backpack on your hips to progress.
busy.why: Bodyweight or a loaded bag: no gym needed
busy.hint: Use reps and a slow tempo (3 seconds down) to make it hard enough. Stop with 2 to 3 reps left.

dumbbellOnly.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift

minimumDay.title: The 10-minute floor
minimumDay.detail: Short on time or energy? Do one round of: 10 squats, 8 push-ups (any version), a 20-second plank, 10 glute bridges. Then 5 minutes of easy stretching. Doing this keeps the habit alive, and a habit is worth more than any single session.

active.restDay: On rest days stretch or do a yoga flow. Light movement helps you recover faster than lying still.

progression.method: Double progression: add reps first, then weight.
rules: Pick a weight where your last rep of your last set still leaves the reps in reserve shown on the exercise.
Each week try to add one rep to each set until every set reaches the top of the range.
Then add the smallest weight step and start again at the bottom of the range. A small step is about 2 kg for upper body and 5 kg for lower body.
If you are 2 or more reps below last time in two sessions in a row, you are tired, not weak. Keep the weight and cut one set for a week.
Write down weight and reps every session. What you can see improving keeps you going.

whenStuck: Weight on the bar has not moved for 3 weeks: check sleep (7 to 9 hours), protein and total calories first.
In a calorie deficit, holding your strength is a win. Do not chase new records every week.
If one exercise stalls, swap it for a variation from its alternatives for 4 to 6 weeks, then come back.
progression.track: Take progress photos in the same light every 4 weeks, and measure your waist every 2 weeks.

busyGym: Do not wait more than 2 minutes for a machine. Take the swap listed under "Machine busy?" on that exercise, or ask "how many sets do you have left?" and work in between their sets.
Keep the same muscle, the same reps and the same effort. Only the equipment changes. Find the weight in two warm-up sets, starting lighter than you think.
Pair two moves that use different muscles (a push with a pull, or upper with lower) and alternate them while the other station is busy. This also saves time.
At peak hours (evenings, Mondays) do the exercises with free stations first and the crowded ones last. The order of the isolation moves does not matter much.
If your gym does not have a machine at all, the swap list gives the dumbbell and bodyweight versions of it. They work the same muscles.
Wipe the seat, return the weights, and keep your phone off the machine between sets. A good gym is a shared place.

Adjustable or fixed dumbbells (filled water cans work in the meantime)
A sturdy bench or chair for step-ups and supported rows

safety.title: Stop and rest if you feel any of these
safety.detail: Sharp or sudden pain, chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual breathlessness, numbness or tingling. Muscle burn and soreness 1 to 2 days later are normal. Joint pain is not.

safety.title: Form before weight
safety.detail: Use a lighter weight and full control. If you are new, ask the gym trainer to check your squat, hinge and press once. Breathe out on the effort and never hold your breath on heavy reps.

safety.title: Eating less means recovering slower
safety.detail: Keep your protein high, sleep 7 to 9 hours, and take your easy week. If you feel weak for several days in a row, eat at maintenance for a week.

safety.title: Home pulling is the hard part
safety.detail: Without a bar or bands, back training is limited. A resistance band set or a doorway pull-up bar is the best first purchase, then adjustable dumbbells.

safety.title: Not medical advice
safety.detail: This is a general program. If you are pregnant, recovering from injury or surgery, or have a health condition, check with your doctor or a physiotherapist first.
